title: Regular and irregular verbs
metaTitle: Irregular Portuguese verbs list: present, perfeito and participle – Reference – icanspeak Portuguese
description: Regular, irregular and vowel-change European Portuguese verbs at a glance: the eu form of the present, the ele/ela form of the pretérito perfeito and the participle, grouped by pattern.
lead: Three forms tell you most of what you need about a Portuguese verb: eu in the present, ele/ela in the pretérito perfeito, and the participle. Verbs that change in the same way are grouped together.

ptBR.note: Brazil writes nós falamos in the perfeito too (Portugal: falámos), and says dirigir where Portugal says conduzir.

sections.name: Regular verbs
sections.what: Take the ending off the infinitive (-ar, -er, -ir) and add the regular endings. Most verbs work like this, and new verbs do too: tuitar, tuitou, tuitado.
regel: Pattern: *falar: falo · falou · falado.* *comer: como · comeu · comido.* *partir: parto · partiu · partido.*
The accent changes the word: *falo* = I speak, *falou* = he or she spoke. In Portugal *nós* has its own perfeito with an accent: *falámos* (we spoke), against the present *falamos*.
-er and -ir verbs share their participle ending: *comido, partido.*
Spelling keeps the sound in the eu form of the perfeito: *ficar → fiquei, chegar → cheguei, começar → comecei.* The ele/ela form stays regular: *ficou, chegou, começou.*
A few verbs have two participles: a regular one after *ter* and a short one after *ser* and *estar*: *aceitado / aceite, entregado / entregue.* See estar + participle.
items: assistir a = to attend; in Brazil also “to watch”.
# Regular, with a spelling change in eu of the perfeito

sections.name: Irregular verbs
sections.what: These change in one or more of the three forms. The most common verbs in Portuguese are here, so learn them first.
regel: Many irregular verbs take a new stem in the perfeito: *ter → teve, fazer → fez, dizer → disse, pôr → pôs, estar → esteve.*
*ser* and *ir* have the same perfeito: *foi, foram.* The sentence tells you which one it is: *Foi médico.* (ser) / *Foi a Lisboa.* (ir)
The eu form can be the only irregular form in the present: *fazer → faço*, but *fazes, faz.*
After *ter*, the participle never changes: *tenho feito, tem escrito, temos visto.*
*pôr* and *pôde* (ele, perfeito of *poder*) keep their circumflex; *pode* (present) has none.
items: eu pude; the accent separates pôde (perfeito) from pode (present).
Brazil: dirigir is the usual verb.
u in the eu form only: cubro, but cobres.

sections.name: Vowel-change and spelling verbs
sections.what: The eu form of the present changes the stem: peço, ouço, durmo. The perfeito and the participle are regular, apart from the verbs of the previous lists.
regel: In many -ir verbs the stem vowel changes in the eu form only: *dormir → durmo* (but *dormes, dorme*), *vestir → visto, preferir → prefiro, sentir → sinto, repetir → repito, seguir → sigo.*
A few change in the other forms instead: *subir → subo, sobes, sobe, sobem.*
Some verbs change a consonant in the eu form: *pedir → peço, ouvir → ouço, perder → perco, medir → meço.* The same stem is used in the present subjunctive (*peça, ouça*).
-ar verbs in -ear and -iar add an i in the singular and in eles: *passear → passeio, passeias, passeia, passeiam.* (*nós passeamos* has none.)
The perfeito and the participle are regular: *pediu, ouviu, dormiu, vestiu; pedido, ouvido, dormido.*
